_meta.indication: Combination of drospirenone (a progestin) and estetrol (an estrogen) indicated for use by females of reproductive potential to prevent pregnancy

pivotal_trials.design: One-year, multicenter, open-label, single-arm phase 3 trial conducted in the US and Canada (77 US sites and 7 Canadian sites)
pivotal_trials.population: Females of reproductive potential aged 16 to 35 years desiring contraception; 1674 participants enrolled
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pearl Index (number of pregnancies per 100 women-years of treatment / per at-risk cycles) in subjects aged 16 to 35 years
pivotal_trials.n: 1524 participants in the primary Pearl Index analysis (of 1674 enrolled)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall Pearl Index 2.65 (95% CI 1.73, 3.88), based on 26 on-treatment pregnancies over 12,673 at-risk cycles in 1524 participants

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (22%): bleeding irregularities, mood disturbance, headache, breast symptoms, dysmenorrhea, acne, weight increased, and libido decreased. Across the two phase 3 trials (N=3632, females 16-50 years of age): mood disturbance 9.1%, bleeding irregularities 10.8%, breast symptoms 5.4%, headache 6.3%. 9.6% discontinued due to an adverse reaction (most frequent: bleeding irregularity 2.8%). Serious risks include thromboembolic disorders and hyperkalemia.
target_moa: Combined hormonal contraceptive whose primary contraceptive mechanism, like other CHCs, is ovulation inhibition; estetrol (E4) selectively binds estrogen receptors ER-alpha and ER-beta with estrogenic activity, while drospirenone is a spironolactone-analogue progestin with anti-mineralocorticoid activity
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination oral tablet of the progestin drospirenone 3 mg and the estrogen estetrol 14.2 mg anhydrous)

boxed_warning.content: Cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events: cigarette smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from CHC use; CHCs including NEXTSTELLIS are contraindicated in females over 35 years of age who smoke

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management determined that a REMS is not necessary for this product

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was needed as no new efficacy or safety concerns outside of those expected for a combined hormonal contraceptive were identified; the application was not referred to an advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary

basis.text: This application received Standard (not Priority) review
